To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the distribution of fermentation products produced by a community is affected by the electron donor fed to that community, and this is due to a change in community activity, not community structure.

the distribution of products from fermentative communities is affected by initial substrate concentration and that the shift in product distribution is due to changes in community function, not community structure.
the microbial community structure and the fermentation products are determined by the electron donor, rather than its concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of electron donor concentration and type on the fermentation of electron donors in anaerobic environments and the microbial community structure that results.
the effects of changing substrate concentration on the microbial community structure and fermentation products produced.
the effect of electron donor concentrations on the microbial community structure and the production of fermentation products.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microbial community structure does not appear to be affected by the concentration of electron donors.

, as electron donor concentration increases, the fraction of the electrons channeled towards methane decreases, while the fraction of the electron channeled towards short chain fatty acids increases, and that this shift in electron flow is caused by a change in microbial community function, rather a change in microbial composition.
the microbial community structure was affected, but the change was substrate dependent and did not correlate with the change in the fermentation product.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a shift in the balance of fermentation end-products is achieved by changing the electron donor provided, and that this shift in the fermentation products does not require a change in the community structure of the anaerobic fermenting community.
the microbial community structure and the fermentation products produced are determined by the electron donor provided, rather than the concentration of that electron donor.
the community is determined by the substrate fed, rather than the concentration of the substrate fed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microbial community structure and the function of the community are differentially affected by the concentration of the electron donor.
the balance of fermentation product formation is controlled by the microbial communities, which in turn is controlled by the substrate provided.
the microbial community structure and the fermentation products are strongly affected by the initial concentration of the electron donor fed to an anaerobic community.
